sentences.text: ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

Heard learned Advocate Mr. Vishal C. Mehta for the Appellant, learned Advocate Mr. Kassh K.
Thakkar for Respondent Nos. 1(1) to 1(6), learned Advocate Mr. Rathin P. Ragal for Respondent No.2.
C/FA/1984/2021 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/01/2023 2.
Learned Advocate Mr. Vishal C. Mehta for the Appellant has submitted that there is an amicable settlement taken place with Respondent Nos. 1(1) to 1(6).
He has placed on record the settlement pursis which is ordered to be taken on record.
However, so longer as Respondent No.2 - The United India Insurance Co. Ltd. is concerned, it is exonerated by the learned Tribunal.
Learned Advocate for the Appellant has further submitted that identical order is passed by the coordinate bench in First Appeal No. 2054 of 2020 on 13.10.2020 arising out of the same accident.
He has therefore urged to pass appropriate order.

3. In support of the statement made by learned Advocate Mr. Vishal C. Mehta, he has placed on record the settlement pursis which reads as under:
"We, the undersigned, the Appellant and the Respondent Nos. 1(1) to 1(6) have amicably settled the dispute / grievances arising in the claim petition being M.A.C.
Petition No. 607 of 2008 as follows:
1. The original Claimants, namely heirs of deceased Jivabhai Samatbhai Chauhan,
have preferred the present claim petition before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Main), Jamnagar (hereinafter referred to as "the Lower Court" for short) seeking compensation in view of the death of Jivabhai Samtabhai Chauhan due to the accident in question, from the Appellant and the Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company.

2. The Lower Court, on dated 28.5.2018, after due deliberations, partly allowed the claim petition preferred by the original Claimants, by awarding a sum of Rs.7,12,600/- as compensation along with the interest at the rate of 9% per annum thereon; however, the Lower Court has fastened the liability to pay the amount of compensation upon the Appellant only and has exonerated the Respondent No.2 - The Insurance Company on the ground that the deceased was travelling as an unauthorized passenger in the offending vehicle.
C/FA/1984/2021 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/01/2023 3.

After passing of the impugned judgment and award, the parties have made sincere efforts to resolve the dispute and, accordingly, the original Claimants are ready and willing to accept an amount of Rs.2,50,000/- as full and final amount towards compensation including the interest and cost and, the Appellant has made payment Khodabhai Togabhai Dangar vs Madhuben Jivrajbhai Chauhan on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133751727/

sentences.text: 2 of Rs.2,50,000/- to the original Claimants on dated 07.11.2022, and the undersigned Claimants are hereby acknowledging the receipts thereof.

4. The undersigned Claimants hereby undertake and assure that they shall not, in future, initiate any further proceedings seeking compensation from the Appellant in respect o the accident in question and they shall accept the total amount of compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- as full and final amount of compensation including the interest and cost as against the awarded amount of Rs.7,12,600/- and the interest at the rate of 9% per annum thereon.
5.

The present Settlement in respect of the compensation for the accident in question is binding upon the original Claimants and their heirs and successors also and they all shall be restrained from initiating any proceedings for seeking any compensation in respect of the death of the deceased due to accident in question against the Appellant, in future.

6. In view of the aforesaid Settlement arrived at between the parties, this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to modify the judgment and award passed by the Lower Court in M.A.C. Petition No.607 of 2008 dated 28.5.2018 to the aforesaid extent and pass an order to the effect that the award passed by the Lower Court stands satisfied in view of the present Settlement and payment already made thereof."
4. In view of the aforesaid factual scenario and in view of the settlement pursis C/FA/1984/2021 JUDGMENT DATED: 17/01/2023 placed on record, the court pass the following order.

4.1 By way of the present appeal, the appellant - owner of the offending vehicle, challenged the judgment and award dated 28.05.2018 passed by the M.A.C.T. (Main), Jamnagar in M.A.C.P.
No.607 of 2008 whereby, the learned Tribunal has awarded amount of compensation of Rs.7,12,600/- with interest.

4.2 It appears that pending hearing of the present appeal, owner of the vehicle and remaining original claimants have settled the matter and the original claimants have shown readiness and willingness to accept the amount of Rs.2,50,000/- as full and final amount towards compensation including the interest and cost.
It appears that the original claimants have received the entire amount of compensation as agreed as per the settlement pursis which is quoted above, which is ordered to be taken on record.

4.3 Learned advocates appearing for the respective parties state at bar that the parties have voluntarily agreed to the settlement pursis and accordingly, the same has been executed before the Notary and thereafter, it has been placed before this Court for its consideration and for disposal of the present appeal.
4. In view of the voluntary character of the settlement pursis as stated at bar by the learned advocates for the respective parties, present appeal is partly allowed.
The claimants are held to be entitled to the agreed sum of Rs.2,50,000/- as compensation including interest and cost.
The impugned award is accordingly modified to the extent as agreed in the settlement pursis.

3 also stated at bar by the original claimants that they have received the agreed amount as per settlement and thus, the impugned award stands fully satisfied and, therefore, the learned Tribunal shall record satisfaction of the award accordingly in a proper manner in the record of the Court.
